clue.text: A stag party's branching out?

parts.note: the stag is the male deer, not a groom's night out, and the branching growth is part of the animal itself

explanation.surface: A bachelor celebration splits up and heads off in different directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stag party' suggests a pre-wedding night out; read literally it is the stag's own part, the one that branches out from its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Each bony branched growth on a deer's head belongs to the stag, so it is a part of that animal which branches.

clue.text: Embraces Oriental wives

parts.note: E, short for East, stands for oriental
wives are spouses

explanation.surface: Someone takes up with Eastern brides.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause or idea is to adopt or take it up, a figurative sense of hug.

clue.text: Here you might eat a true 2 stark green salad

indicators.note: a salad is a tossed mixture, so the letters of these words are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner is offered a plain, entirely green salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salad' rearranges A TRUE STARK GREEN. The stray '2' in the clue gives no letters and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant is a place for meals, here one serving Hellenic food.

clue.text: The sort of person who would destroy a beautiful dish

definitions.text: The sort of person who would destroy

explanation.surface: A hooligan breaks an attractive plate.
explanation.definitionFit: One who breaks things to pieces; also British slang for a very attractive person, as 'dish' is slang for a good-looking one.

clue.text: Tongue to which 3 patrons may be treated

definitions.text: Tongue to which 3 patrons may be treated

parts.words: Tongue to which 3 patrons may be treated
parts.note: diners at the eatery of 3 down may hear the waiters speaking Greek, a speech from abroad, and 'treated' hints at a meal of tongue

explanation.surface: Customers at an eatery are served tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like a dish on the menu; it means a language, the one the diners at the Hellenic eatery of 3 down hear spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and one from another country is spoken abroad.

clue.text: He noted that Annie should get her gun in Germany

definitions.text: He noted that Annie should get her gun

explanation.surface: A man insists Annie must arm herself while in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Irving Berlin wrote the songs (the notes) of the musical 'Annie Get Your Gun'; the capital city shares his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin composed the musical about Annie Oakley; the German capital is a city in that country.

clue.text: Study first letter in chapter head

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the word for a study

parts.note: a den is a private study room
A is the first letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone researches the opening letter of a book's section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chapter' is not a book section here but a cathedral's body of clergy, which a dean heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral chapter, its body of canons, is led by its senior cleric.

clue.text: Guns going off across the veldt?

definitions.text: Guns going off across the veldt?

indicators.note: something going off goes wrong or bad, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rifles are fired out on the African grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' reads as firing; it rearranges GUNS, and the whole clue pictures antelope careering across South African grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest are antelope herding across the open grassland of southern Africa.

clue.text: A sailor-soldier about to strike

indicators.note: the marine abbreviation is placed around the letter

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marine, a soldier who serves at sea

explanation.surface: A marine is about to hit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram is to strike with force, as a ship hits another.

clue.text: Tin one for a starter?

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a tin as the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool for a can is a tin-type device; also the first item, as a batsman opening an innings or a first course.

clue.text: A recess for the company to tuck into minced veal

indicators.note: the company abbreviation is tucked inside the other letters
minced meat is chopped up, so the letters of veal are rearranged

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Guests at a firm's dinner eat minced veal in a nook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tuck into' looks like eating; it puts CO inside ALVE, the letters of VEAL rearranged by 'minced'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a niche set back into a wall.

clue.text: Sow heather to be planted out later

parts.note: to sow is to seed
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: A gardener sows heather to move to the border later.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the young plant; LING is a name for the common heather of British moors.
explanation.definitionFit: A young plant raised from seed is grown in a tray before transplanting outdoors.

clue.text: Kept hot sweet from China?

parts.note: kept as in conserved means preserved
ginger is hot and spicy

explanation.surface: Something spicy is saved for later as a Chinese treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the confection is typically associated with China, not only from there.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem root in syrup, sold in jars, is a traditional Chinese confection.

clue.text: You sound like Mrs 9

indicators.note: signals that the word must be said out loud

parts.note: the pronoun as spoken

explanation.surface: Someone is told they resemble Mrs Ram.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is RAM, so his wife is the female sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is the mate of a male one, playfully called his missus.

clue.text: Persevere, troubled Sir, in faltering step

indicators.note: the troubled letters go inside the faltering ones
a faltering step stumbles out of order, so its letters are rearranged
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of sir are mixed up

explanation.surface: A distressed knight is urged to keep going despite his stumbling walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' turns SIR into RSI, which 'in' puts inside PEST, the rearrangement of STEP from 'faltering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to carry on resolutely in spite of difficulty.

clue.text: The first person to go after mare's tail

indicators.note: the verb comes after the letter
the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go behind a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first person' is the self, 'I', as in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: The self, which speaks in the grammatical first person, is the 'I'.

clue.text: A lot of gas and froth after bottle opening

indicators.note: the foam word follows the letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lather is froth

explanation.surface: A bottle is opened and fizzes over with foam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' is idle chatter, not vapour; B, the opening letter of 'bottle', is followed by LATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-winded nonsense talk is chatter, much as 'gassing' means chattering.

clue.text: Time Out's acrobatic bird

indicators.note: an acrobat tumbles, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A listings magazine features an agile bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Time Out is a London listings magazine; 'acrobatic' rearranges TIMEOUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tit, a small songbird, is also called by this longer name.

clue.text: She isn't bitter about the German muddle

parts.note: mild and bitter are two kinds of British beer, so mild is the one that is not bitter

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: der is German for the

explanation.surface: A sweet-natured woman is upset by a German mix-up.
explanation.walkthrough: MILD and BITTER are two British pub beers; DER, the German for 'the', is rearranged by 'muddle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name answers 'She'.

clue.text: The crowning jewel Edward first brought to England?

parts.note: a coronation is a crowning
a gem is a stone

explanation.surface: A gem in a crown is shipped to England by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward I took the Stone of Scone from Scotland to England in 1296; it sits beneath the throne at coronations.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward I seized the Scottish Stone of Scone, used at crowning ceremonies, and took it to Westminster.

clue.text: Where nurses are going ahead

explanation.surface: Hospital staff carry on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurses work on a hospital ward; as one word it means forward, advancing.

clue.text: They may hit ears when nose is out of joint

indicators.note: something out of joint is dislocated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets a punch on the ears when their nose is put out of joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of joint' rearranges NOSE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounds reach and strike the ear.

clue.text: Transfixed with the prospect of being given a grilling

definitions.text: with the prospect of being given a grilling

explanation.surface: A suspect freezes at the prospect of interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a grilling' sounds like an interrogation; meat put on a kebab stick is about to be grilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierced through with a pointed rod, as kebab meat is before going under the grill.

clue.text: Break stones in sound sleep

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone breaks rocks while deeply asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'deep'; it is the homophone signal, the K being silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape flint or stone by striking it is to knap.

clue.text: I put a ring around an ideal place on More's map

definitions.text: an ideal place on More's map

indicators.note: around means roundabout, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: a ring is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone circles a perfect spot on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas More named his imaginary ideal island in his 1516 book.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imaginary perfect commonwealth gave its name to any ideal society.

clue.text: Influential supporter giving a touch of encouragement to Reagan

parts.note: a pat on the back is an encouraging touch
Ron is short for Ronald, the first name of President Reagan

explanation.surface: An ally gives President Reagan an encouraging pat.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer or sponsor gives support, often money, to an artist or cause.

clue.text: Work unit in Bergen

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the Norwegian city name

explanation.surface: A team works in the Norwegian port.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, the CGS unit of work or energy.

clue.text: She would drop

explanation.surface: A woman wishes she could let something fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraction of 'she had/would'; also to cast off, as trees lose leaves.
